articles.title: Delhi govt mulls hike in agricultural land circle rates, proposals up to ₹5 crore per acre - CNBC TV18
articles.full_text:
Delhi govt mulls hike in agricultural land circle rates, proposals up to ₹5 crore per acre
The Delhi administration is overhauling agricultural land valuations frozen for nearly two decades to bridge massive gaps with prevailing market prices. This strategic adjustment aims to reshape future property deals and urban development under long-term planning frameworks. Discover how officials intend to address stark price disparities across high-value suburban belts.
The Delhi government is considering revising circle rates for agricultural land, which have remained unchanged since 2008, with proposals recommending rates of up to ₹5 crore per acre in some districts, according to sources.
The proposed revision, being examined by the Centre and the Delhi government, seeks to align official land valuations with prevailing market prices and could have implications for land transactions, property development and urban expansion under the Master Plan for Delhi-2047.

Sources said that in a recent meeting of the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry and the Delhi government, the proposed circle rates were discussed in detail.
The exercise follows a public consultation initiated through a notice issued on October 1, 2025. A committee was formed in July this year to examine gaps in the existing valuation framework and recommend changes.
The current indicative circle rate for agricultural land is ₹53 lakh per acre, while the rate for agricultural land in floodplain areas stands at ₹17.6 lakh per acre.
Under the proposals, agricultural land circle rates could be fixed at ₹5 crore per acre in South and New Delhi districts, ₹3 crore in North, West and North-West districts, and ₹2.5 crore in Central Delhi.

For instance, in South Delhi, market rates reportedly range from ₹1.5 crore to ₹10 crore per acre, with Chhattarpur and the farmhouse belt among the higher-value areas.
In Najafgarh, prices range from ₹3 crore to ₹10 crore per acre, while green-belt and rural land is valued at ₹2 crore to ₹8 crore, they said.
In New Delhi district, market rates reportedly range from ₹1.5 crore to ₹18 crore per acre, reflecting variations in location and property category, sources added.
